So the live question was whether 'Otherwise' first appeared in Constance (1993) and the source names the wrong volume. It did not. Three independent confirmations: the Library of Congress Poetry 180 credit reprints it by permission of Graywolf Press from Otherwise: New and Selected Poems; Journey with Jesus gives the same book, Graywolf, 1996; and Words for the Year carries the copyright line 'Copyright 1996 by the Estate of Jane Kenyon', which is the decisive one, since a poem carried over from Constance would sit under a 1993 copyright. The book description confirms the structure the locator depends on: twenty new poems open the volume, selected and arranged by Kenyon shortly before her death in April 1995, followed by selections from From Room to Room, The Boat of Quiet Hours, Let Evening Come and Constance. So 'the new poems' in the locator is right and the named edition is the first book appearance.
